description: Anonymised customer key: the letter C and five digits (C00001 to C05000). It is unique per row and is not linked to a name, phone number or email, so it is not personal data on its own.
Age band of the customer: 18-25, 26-35, 36-45, 46-55 or 55+. A band is stored instead of the exact age to protect privacy.
Sales region of the customer's registered address: North, South, East, West or Central.
Number of purchases (orders) the customer made in the observation period. Whole number from 1 to 48. This is the Frequency input of RFM.
Average value of one order in Indian rupees (INR), 2 decimals, between 100 and 25,000. Monetary value in RFM is purchase_freq multiplied by avg_order_value.
Days since the customer's last purchase, counted at the snapshot date. Whole number from 1 to 365; lower means more recent. This is the Recency input of RFM.
Current loyalty points balance, whole number from 0 to 9,999. In the generated rows it is about 1 point per INR 100 spent; HCL's original rows do not follow that relation.
1 if the customer has stopped buying (churned), 0 if still active. This is the label the churn model predicts. About 15% of rows are 1.

Customer segment from the shared RFM rule: quintile scores 1-5 for recency, frequency and spend, then Champion (R>=4 and F>=4), Loyal, New, At_Risk or Lost. Recomputed over the cleaned rows, so it matches the segment the app shows.
